title: Simulate confidence interval widths at pre-specified assurance
code: library(precisionSim)

title: Simulate confidence interval widths at pre-specified assurance
text: ’ll use sleepstudy data lme4 package, create simple model. practice, pilot data another (related) study.
code: #get data data_sleep <- lme4::sleepstudy  #create model mod1 <- lme4::lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1|Subject), data = data_sleep)

title: Simulate confidence interval widths at pre-specified assurance
text: need create custom function take lme4 model input, produces data.frame columns ‘estimand’, ‘estimate’, ‘lower’, ‘upper’. , just beta coefficient ‘Task’: can quickly test function follows: Note instance one estimand, multiple estimands can produced adding rows outputs data frame. popular choices estimands may marginal means pairwise contrasts (e.g., derived emmeans package).
code: #define function to get interval of interest interval_function <- function(fitted_model){    ci <- suppressMessages(confint(fitted_model))    return(     data.frame(       estimand = "Days",       estimate = lme4::fixef(fitted_model)[[2]],       lower = ci[4,1],       upper = ci[4,2]     )   )  } interval_function(mod1) #>   estimand estimate    lower    upper #> 1     Days 10.46729 8.886551 12.04802

title: Simulate confidence interval widths at pre-specified assurance
text: ’d normally run 100 simulations (e.g., 5000), simplicity efficiency just run 100
code: #run 100 simulations for ease (should be higher for the real thing e.g., 5000) sim1 <- precisionSim(mod1,                      target_width = c(3,4,5), #different widths to test                      interval_fun = interval_function, #our custom function                      prob = 0.80, #assurance probability                      mc_conf_level = 0.95, #monte carlo confidence level for our probability                       nsim = 100, #number of simulations, usually go higher (e.g., 5000)                      seed = 123) #seed #> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'car': #>   method           from #>   na.action.merMod lme4  #summary summary(sim1) #> Precision analysis by simulation #> =============================== #>  #> Model: Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject)  #> Simulations requested: 100  #> Target probability: 80 % #> Monte Carlo confidence level: 95 % #>  #>  Estimand Width Assurance Monte Carlo CI #>  Days     3     15%       8.65%, 23.53%  #>  Days     4     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  Days     5     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  #> Diagnostics: #>   Failed fits: 0  #>   Non-converged fits: 0  #>   Singular fits: 0  #>   Interval failures: 0  #>  #> Elapsed time: 169.916

title: Simulate confidence interval widths at pre-specified assurance
text: can visualise results two ways: 1) “assurance” ecdf, 2) “distribution” shows histogram simulated widths.
code: #visualise plot(sim1, type="assurance") plot(sim1, type="distribution") #> `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

title: Simulate confidence interval widths at pre-specified assurance
text: can also take results, determine confidence interval width pre-specified assurance probability.
code: #determine widths at 50%, 75% and 90% assurance levels quantile(sim1, prob = c(0.5, 0.75, 0.9)) #>           50%      75%     90% #> Days 3.160141 3.280826 3.35031

text: need create custom function take lme4 model input, produces data.frame columns ‘estimand’, ‘estimate’, ‘lower’, ‘upper’. , just beta coefficient ‘Task’: can quickly test function follows: Note instance one estimand, multiple estimands can produced adding rows outputs data frame.
code: #define function to get interval of interest interval_function <- function(fitted_model){    ci <- suppressMessages(confint(fitted_model))    return(     data.frame(       estimand = "Days",       estimate = lme4::fixef(fitted_model)[[2]],       lower = ci[4,1],       upper = ci[4,2]     )   )  } interval_function(mod1) #>   estimand estimate    lower    upper #> 1     Days 10.46729 8.886551 12.04802

title: Simulate confidence interval widths at multiple sample sizes
text: ’d normally run 100 simulations (e.g., 5000), simplicity efficiency just run 100 can see hit n=30, lowest confidence interval width 3 achieved 100% time.
code: #run 100 simulations for ease (should be higher for the real thing e.g., 5000) sim1 <- precisionCurve(mod_extended,                      target_width = c(3,4,5), #different widths to test                      interval_fun = interval_function, #our custom function                      along = "Subject", #variable were are simulating along                      breaks = c(20, 30, 40), #number of levels of 'Subject' to simulate                      prob = 0.80, #assurance probability                      mc_conf_level = 0.95, #monte carlo confidence level for our probability                       nsim = 100, #number of simulations, usually go higher (e.g., 5000)                      seed = 123) #seed  #summary summary(sim1) #> Precision analysis by simulation #> =============================== #>  #> Model: Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject)  #> Simulations requested: 100  #> Target probability: 80 % #> Monte Carlo confidence level: 95 % #>  #>  Estimand nlevels nrow Width Assurance Monte Carlo CI #>  Days     20      200  3     47%       36.94%, 57.24% #>  Days     20      200  4     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  Days     20      200  5     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  Days     30      300  3     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  Days     30      300  4     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  Days     30      300  5     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  Days     40      400  3     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  Days     40      400  4     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  Days     40      400  5     100%      96.38%, 100%   #>  #> Diagnostics: #>   Failed fits: 0  #>   Non-converged fits: 0  #>   Singular fits: 0  #>   Interval failures: 0  #>  #> Elapsed time: 501.554

title: Estimate Sample Size For Linear Mixed Models Based On Precision
text: Basic installation can done via install_github() function remotes package. installed, can load library use various functions.
code: #install the package remotes::install_github("Kneerav/precisionSim") library(precisionSim)

title: Estimate Sample Size For Linear Mixed Models Based On Precision
code: library(lme4) library(precisionSim)  #create model mod1 <- lmer(peak_force ~ task + (1|participant), data=fake_data)  #define function that extracts the interval of interest interval_function <- function(fitted_model){    #fit emmeans   em_df <- emmeans::emmeans(fitted_model, pairwise ~ task)    #get ci   ci <- as.data.frame(     confint(       em_df$contrasts, level = 0.95, adjust="none"     )   )    #return object   return(     data.frame(       estimand = ci$contrast,       estimate = ci$estimate,       lower = ci$lower.CL,       upper = ci$upper.CL     )   ) }  #run precision sim sim1 <- precisionSim(   fit = mod1,   target_width = c(0.1, 0.2),   interval_fun = interval_function,   prob = 0.80,   mc_conf_level = 0.95,   nsim = 100,   seed = 123456,   singular_action = "include",   nonconverged_action = "exclude",   tol = 1e-4 )  #check summary(sim1)  #plot plot(sim1, type="assurance")  #plot plot(sim1, type="distribution")  #recheck quantiles quantile(sim1, prob = c(0.5, 0.8))
